v: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
As he began the settlements, a debtor owing ten thousand talents was brought to him.
Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.
Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.
But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’
So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’
But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.
When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.
Then the master summoned him and said, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.
Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’
In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.
That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”

paras: One day one of the closest followers of Jesus came to Him and asked, “Lord, if someone keeps doing wrong to me, how many times do I have to forgive him? Up to seven times?”
And Jesus said, “Not just seven times. Every single time!” And then Jesus told them a story to explain what the Kingdom of God is like.
There was a king who wanted to collect all the money that his servants owed him. And a servant who owed the king billions of dollars was brought before him.
Well, the servant couldn’t pay it back. So the king ordered that the servant, his family, and everything he owned be sold to pay off the debt.

The servant fell on his knees and begged the king, “Please, be patient with me, and I’ll pay you back everything!” The king felt so sorry for him, so he forgave his whole debt and let the servant go free.

But when this servant left, he found another servant who owed him several thousand dollars. And the first servant grabbed the second servant by the throat and started choking him, and he said, “Pay me back what you owe me!”

And the second servant fell down and begged him, “Please, be patient with me, and I’ll pay you back!” But the first servant refused and had the second servant thrown into prison until he could pay the debt.
When the king’s other servants saw what happened, they were incredibly upset. So they went and told the king everything.

So the king called the first servant back in and said, “You evil servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me. Shouldn’t you have mercy on that other servant, just like I had mercy on you?!?!”
Then the king handed the first servant over to the jailers to be tortured until he paid back everything he owed.
Then Jesus said, “That is how my Father in heaven will treat each one of you, unless you forgive others from your heart.”
